reviews.title: Completely Inaccessible For Voiceover Users!
reviews.text: I’ve been asking the developers of CityMapper to please follow access guidelines when developing their app, they have not and will not by the looks. It is rare to find such intransigence within the App Developer Community, especially Apples one as Apple give developers so much information on how to make their apps accessible to the widest number of users. CityMapper should note that there are a number of us who have fiercer lived experience of disability and where companies refuse to follow access requirements. We often serve within areas of public life in which we can influence division making processes around what apps are adopted. This is especially true where public transport providers have legal duty around accessibility and the Equality Act etc.

reviews.title: Inconsistent when you need it most
reviews.text: I’ve been using Citymapper for years and have preferred it over every other mapping app. However, there have been multiple times where the directions have been so bad that I got completely lost or stranded and I had to delete it. But I prefer the user interface more than other apps so I redownloaded it over and over. But the inconsistency of the information has gone too far. Telling me trains are going to places they aren’t, sending me to different boroughs, doubling or even tripling how long it takes me to get to my destination. I need an app I can trust and unfortunately I can’t trust Citymapper.

reviews.title: Artificially Boosting Ads Metric
reviews.text: They artificially increase their metric on engagement with their ads by doing the following. I’ve noticed that even when I am very positive I have not actually clicked the ads, it pops up. I suspect they enlarge the actual range or sensitivity of the ads beyond the actual image/real estate of the ads, to increase the clickability of the ads artificially — this makes users believe they inadvertently clicked on the ads and so they can artificially boost ad engagement numbers to charge more for ad space. Gaslighting users into believing they inadvertently clicked ads in order to make an “optional” ad a mandatory one is really deceptive. Useful app, but please don’t treat users like fools. One too many suspicious “inadvertent” clicks later, here I am.

reviews.title: Worst app ever with no walk option on iwatch!!
reviews.text: This is the worst app ever!!  I got a new iwatch so I could see the step by step directions on city mapper walking options, which is possible on the phone but not on the watch?!??  This is a ridiculous oversight and the developers should be ashamed of themselves for not thinking of adding a walk option on the watch companion app or to have it sync at least with the iPhone app, but it doesn’t work!! So it remembers the location but it only will tell you the bus route to take on the watch, even when the phone version is guiding you on the walking route which is what it’s supposed to do!!!  Negative stars!!!

reviews.title: Great app but unhappy about them selling user data
reviews.text:
You have tried to gamify the app to much. As such paid users have not materialised. Now you have to sell user data to who knows what. 

I paid for a premium subscription but the value was not there. Come on guy! do not go down the route of selling our data. Just create a product people are willing to pay for. Just use an AI bot to brainstorm some ideas.

Or even better just ask users what they want and built it. I would love to be able to have a Journal for trip notes and planning. I would love to have Wikipedia and similar articles I can read in the app before I get to my destination. You guys can partner with money suppermarket and during commute give users opens to switch their energy supplier. I would love to have To Do’s in the app so when I commute I know that I have X minutes to get things done and the app can tell me you have 20 minutes till your destination. Why dont you get 2-3 tasks done and free up your day. You can partner with Waze so whenever users drive cars they still have the ecosystem the same way. 

Please be an innovative company and do not just search for the lazy way out and sell all our data to strange companies. 

From: former paid user, former iOS app user (using your app now only via browsers that allow me to manage strictly cookies and connections).

reviews.title: This was great... now not so much..AND now all saved routes just deleted!!
reviews.text:
Well, it’s good UNLESS YOU KNOW THE CITY! Then you know the routes are not the best ones! 
I have no idea what’s happened but the routes make no sense anymore. If you don’t know they city you’re in this would probably screw you. Standing next to Dalston Junction station and I know a train to brockley leaves in 5 mins and will take me 20 mins to get home. However Citymapper in all its wisdom wants to send me on 3 trains and a bus via London bridge for no reason at all!! So stupid.
 Other routes also not making sense... I want to have to brockley to London Bridge trains come up as I prefer that route.. but they dont even appear if there isn’t one in the next 10 mins (which there usually isn’t as they aren’t as regular now). Just stupid.
NOT TO MENTION NOW IN JUNE 2036 it has deleted all saved routes!! I needed them because the routes it gives me are usually wrong! It can’t even decide which is my closest station and sends me to one further away!!

reviews.title: Borderline useless as a public transit user
reviews.text:
The app goes out of their way to hide bus routes. It’ll decide that a route is too short for anyone to possibly want to take the bus. It’s 85° and I’m getting groceries, I’m not walking a mile each way, I want the bus schedule! Want to know when the next bus is coming? They don’t want to tell you! It prioritizes telling you how many minutes until they think you’ll be there. I don’t care! If I’m looking for the next bus I want to knew when it’s picking me up so I can plan when to leave, but that’s hidden within the app.

I’m now without food for the week because this app has caused me to miss my appointment at the food bank.

reviews.title: Bus timings
reviews.text: I don’t know if it’s not this app’s fault or what. But it always shows wrong times of buses especially slough to Windsor. If it’s saying bus is at 6:20 then bus will arrive at 6:08 or 9 something and then it suddenly changed the time on the app as well. That doesn’t make sense like I start getting ready and doing everything after checking time on app. And if it changes anything it ruin my whole schedule sometimes I’m late for my work. Today 21 December on Sunday it was saying bus timing at 6:28am and I was at bus stop at 6:18am and then the bus came (703) at 6:59am. Like what is it I can’t understand if there’s not any bus in morning why this app showing me while I’m at my home. Really upset I had to kept standing on bus stop for almost 40mins in this weather when it’s super cold and dark outside. Rubbish app
